tools.name: doctor

tools.description:
Run platform, release, installed Pane, daemon reachability, runpane-on-PATH, and remote setup diagnostics.
Use this first when an agent needs to understand whether Pane is installed, which wrapper/runtime is running, what daemon endpoint is expected, and whether the running Pane app is reachable. JSON mode should return a report even when the daemon is unreachable.
Agents should run `doctor` before mutating Pane state.
The JSON report includes daemon reachability as data; an unreachable daemon is not a reason to skip the rest of the report.
Use `agent_context` (in the "admin" toolset) after doctor when full CLI context is needed.
Returns the JSON of `doctor`.

tools.name: repos_list
tools.title: runpane repos list
tools.description:
List repositories saved in the running Pane app.
Use this to find the right Pane-managed repository before creating panes. If the repo is missing, use `repos add` first.
Requires a running Pane app or daemon for the selected Pane data directory.
If this fails from WSL with a missing `/tmp/pane-daemon.../daemon.sock`, `volta: command not found`, or a Windows shim error, the user may be running Windows Pane. Retry with `/mnt/c/Users/<you>/.pane/bin/runpane repos list --json`, or with an older Pane build `powershell.exe -NoProfile -Command 'Set-Location $env:TEMP; runpane repos list --json'`.
When using PowerShell from WSL, set a Windows cwd such as `$env:TEMP` or `$env:USERPROFILE` before running runpane to avoid UNC cwd issues.

tools.name: secrets_request
tools.title: runpane secrets request
tools.description:
Ask the person for a secret on a masked card. Pane saves what they type as a Pane secret and never returns it.
Shows a Notify card with your title and reason, a masked field, Save securely and Decline. What the person types is saved on this machine as the Pane secret <project>/<name> and synced to their other machines. You get back {status: "saved", project, name} or {status: "declined"}, never the value. Then use it with `runpane secrets exec`.
A result of {waiting: true, id} means the card is still open and your client would otherwise time out: call `notify` with resume: <id> right away to keep waiting.
A result of {unavailable, next} means nobody can answer through Pane right now. Do not ask for the secret in the chat; follow next.
Saving replaces a secret that already exists under that name; the card says so.
Returns the JSON of `secrets_request`.

tools.name: secrets_lease
tools.title: runpane secrets lease
tools.description:
Ask the person to lease 1Password-backed Pane secrets to this machine for a while. Returns the lease's id, end time and machines, never a value.
For secrets that come from 1Password. Shows a lease card with the names, their 1Password references, the machines (by default the person's desktop and this machine), the length and the end time. The person presses Start lease on their computer, Pane reads 1Password once, and each machine keeps the values until the lease ends. You get back {status: "leased", project, names, leaseId, expiresAt, machines} or {status: "declined"}, never a value. Then use them with `runpane secrets exec`.
Only the person approves a lease, on their computer. You can ask for and end leases, never grant or extend one.
A result of {waiting: true, id} means the card is still open and your client would otherwise time out: call `notify` with resume: <id> right away to keep waiting.
A result of {unavailable, next} means nobody can answer through Pane right now; follow next.
About an hour before a lease ends (a quarter of its length for leases shorter than 4 hours), Pane shows the person an Extend card. If the lease ends, `secrets exec` fails with SECRET_LEASE_ENDED and names this command as the next step.
Returns the JSON of `secrets_lease`.

tools.name: device_open
tools.title: runpane devices open
tools.description:
Boot a phone simulator or emulator for this Pane and show its live screen in a device tab beside the agent.
Leases a device to the calling tab's Pane and boots it. Without --device, Pane uses its own device (Pane iPhone or Pane_Android) and makes one from the newest installed runtime when needed. The first call on a machine installs Pane's device tools (agent-device and Expo's device hub), which takes a minute. When every device Pane may boot is held by another Pane, it waits up to 60 seconds, then fails with ERR_DEVICE_BUSY naming the holder. On a machine without Xcode, iOS opens on a linked Mac. Later device calls act on this device; you never pass it again.
Acts only for the Pane of the calling tab: a call from outside a Pane tab, or for a device another Pane holds, is refused. Settings > Devices > Agent device tools turns these tools off.
Returns the JSON of `device_open`.

tools.name: device_run

tools.description:
Run a command where this Pane's device runs, such as a build (npx expo run:ios) or Metro with --background.
On this machine it runs in the Pane's worktree. When the device runs on a linked Mac, Pane first syncs the worktree there (uncommitted changes included) and runs in Pane's checkout on the Mac. Pass an empty command to sync only.
Acts only for the Pane of the calling tab: a call from outside a Pane tab, or for a device another Pane holds, is refused. Settings > Devices > Agent device tools turns these tools off.
Returns the JSON of `device_run`.

tools.name: panes_adopt
tools.title: runpane panes adopt
tools.description:
Adopt an existing externally managed git worktree as a Pane without changing the worktree.
Validates that the canonical path is a registered worktree of the selected saved repository, then creates a Pane record without creating, syncing, building, removing, or recreating the directory.
The resume command is staged without Enter unless --launch is passed.
Archiving never deletes an adopted worktree unless `panes_archive` with removeWorktree: true is used.
One of --agent or --tool-command is required.
With --tool-command, --agent names the agent the command runs (a wrapper such as `agent-farm run`): Pane launches the command unchanged and treats the panel as that agent. Without --agent, Pane detects Claude Code, Codex and Cursor from the foreground process or the agent's screen, and --wait-ready waits for the detected agent's input box; a command that never shows a supported agent is not ready and nothing is typed into it.
--resume needs a built-in agent command; a wrapper command resumes its own way.
The adopted Pane reports `status: running` in `panes list` while its tool terminal is live.
A prompt (--prompt, --initial-input, --prompt-file, --initial-input-file) or --wait-ready needs --launch; without it adopt fails instead of dropping the prompt.
With --launch the result carries the same readiness, initialInput, and nextCommand fields as panes create. With --resume the prompt goes to the resumed conversation's composer once the agent is ready.
To start new work on a named branch, prefer `panes create --base <ref> --branch <name>` over `git worktree add` plus adopt.
Returns the JSON of `panes_adopt`.

tools.name: panes_archive
tools.title: runpane panes archive
tools.description:
Archive a Pane (session) exactly like the UI Archive action, including safe removal of its Pane-managed git worktree, or archive every merged Pane in a Session.
Use this to close out a Pane once its PR has merged. The safety check refreshes the configured upstream before comparing it to HEAD and includes exact unpushed commit IDs and subjects. When the branch has no upstream or its upstream is gone (GitHub deletes merged branches), a merged pull request whose head is HEAD counts as pushed, so squash-merged branches archive without --force. Refuses unsafe archive operations unless --force is used. Use --dry-run to inspect the same evidence without mutating Pane state. Use --session <id|name> --merged to close out every finished Pane of a Session at once. Archive also refuses a Pane with an agent mid-turn or waiting for an answer (`agent-busy`, listed in `safetyCheck.busyAgents`), or with a tab holding unsent composer text or unsaved editor edits (`unsent-input`, listed in `safetyCheck.unsentInput`), unless --force is used, since archiving stops the agent or loses the input. Add --closed to the Session sweep to also archive Panes whose PR closed without merging.
If the result has ok:false with a blocked field, the pane was NOT archived; inspect blocked.code and rerun with --force if discarding the flagged work is intentional.
Inspect safetyCheck.unpushedCommitDetails for exact commit IDs and subjects; upstreamRefreshed confirms the tracking ref was refreshed first.
A --dry-run result sets dryRun:true and wouldArchive without deleting the Pane or its worktree.
A successful archive reports worktreeCleanup `completed` once the worktree is gone from its path and from git. trashDeletion `pending` means a large worktree (for example one with node_modules) is still being deleted from .git/pane-trash in the background; that is still ok:true. `timeout` (also ok:true) means removal is still running; only `failed` sets ok:false.
safetyCheck.mergedViaPr names the merged PR whose head is HEAD; it needs an authenticated `gh`. Without it, a squash-merged branch whose remote branch was deleted reports unpushed-commits.
An adopted Pane (panes adopt) keeps its worktree unless --remove-worktree is passed. `panes restore` does not recreate a removed adopted worktree; the local branch is kept, so `git worktree add <path> <branch>` brings it back.
With --session --merged, each item has outcome archived, would-archive (dry run), skipped (with skipped.code and skipped.message), or failed.
Archiving a main-repo Pane (no Pane-managed worktree) always succeeds immediately since nothing is deleted from disk.
Undo an archive with `panes_restore` with pane: <pane-id>, yes: true, which recreates the worktree. `links_create` with pane: <pane-id> gives the user a link to review the Pane first.
When the safety check is skipped, `safetyCheck.reason` says why: `external-worktree` (an adopted Pane whose worktree Pane does not own), `main-repo`, `missing-project-context`, or `git-error`. `worktreeWillRemain: true` means archiving leaves the worktree on disk.

tools.description:
Open a new agent or terminal tab inside an existing Pane, sharing its worktree. The default for review, QA, fixes and any other agent on work that already has a Pane.
This is the default way to start any later agent on work that already has a Pane, including reviewers, follow-up reviewers, auditors, fix implementers, QA and clean-context helpers. The new tab is a fresh agent that shares the Pane's worktree and branch; it does not create a new worktree. Review, audit and QA tabs never run `git checkout`, `reset` or `stash`, and a fix tab starts only after the previous writer has stopped. Use `panes create` only when the work's branch has no Pane yet. Agent/orchestrator-created panels should pass --source agent or --no-focus so the user stays in the implementation tab. The daemon initializes the terminal immediately and can wait for CLI readiness.
Use this for same-pane reviewer loops after PR creation/testing.
Panels share the existing Pane's worktree and branch.
`panels create` is for visible helper/reviewer tabs, not the agent's default private delegation mechanism.
For agent-created panels, prefer --source agent or --no-focus to avoid stealing focus from the user or implementation tab.
With --tool-command, --agent names the agent the command runs (a wrapper such as `agent-farm run`): Pane launches the command unchanged and treats the panel as that agent. Without --agent, Pane detects Claude Code, Codex and Cursor from the foreground process or the agent's screen, and --wait-ready waits for the detected agent's input box; a command that never shows a supported agent is not ready and nothing is typed into it.
`--chat` or `--agent-farm` creates a chat tab: --initial-input is its first prompt, sent once when the conversation starts; --wait-ready waits for the agent to start. `panels submit`, `wait`, `screen`, `output`, `last-message`, `report` and `resume` work on chat tabs; `panels input` and `submit-composer` do not.

It shows the user a page, plan, report, or dev server as a tab beside the agent, where they are already working.
Write plans and reports as self-contained HTML files. Use --url with a file URL to render a page in a live browser, or --file to open its editable source; reopening the same target reuses its tab.
When the user views Pane from another computer, a file page loads only files in its own folder and the folders inside it. tools.name: panels_close
tools.title: runpane panels close
tools.description:
Close a tab an agent opened, exactly like closing it in Pane; refuses the person's tabs, busy agents and unsent input unless --force.
Closes a tab through the same path as closing it in Pane, so a terminal tab's process stops. It never archives the Pane or touches its worktree. Only a tab an agent opened can close: Pane records the opener when a tab is opened with `--source agent` (panels open, panels create, panes create, agents start). It refuses, without closing, a tab not opened by an agent (the person's, and every tab from before Pane recorded openers), a permanent tab, an agent mid-turn or waiting for an answer, unsent composer text or unsaved editor edits, and a live tab whose input Pane cannot read (agents other than Claude and Codex, and chat tabs). A refusal exits 1 with `refused.code`, `refused.message` and `refused.next`. A tab id that no longer exists returns `alreadyClosed: true`. `--dry-run` reports the same without closing. `--force` (only for a stuck tab, or one the person asked you to close) closes it anyway, as the tab's close button does: a busy agent's turn and unsent input are lost, and the result says `forced: true`. A permanent tab still stays.
ok:false with `refused` means the tab was NOT closed. `refused.code` is opened-by-user, permanent, agent-busy, unsent-input, or input-unknown; follow `refused.next`. Use --force only when the tab is stuck or the person asked you to close it.
`alreadyClosed: true` (ok:true, closed:false) means no tab has that id any more.
With --dry-run, `wouldClose` says whether the close would go ahead and `refused` says why not. Nothing closes; a refused dry run also exits 1.
Open tabs with `--source agent` so they count as yours; `panels list` shows who opened each tab as `openedBy`.

If interrupting a running process, send Ctrl-C first, validate/read output, then send the next command in a separate `panels input` call so bytes are not dropped.
After sending input, validate with `panels_output` with panel: <panel-id> (in the "panels" toolset) before reporting success.
Runpane records action metadata and errors for observability, but should not log full input text by default.
For ordinary text plus Enter, prefer `panels submit` so the terminal receives a CR Enter byte.

tools.description:
Ask the person a question, or tell them something, wherever they are, and get their answer back.
Asks the person through Pane: to pick between options (ui options), to approve or deny an action (ui approve), to type a short answer (ui ask), or tells them something that needs no answer (ui info). Pane shows it on screen even while the person works in another app, and the call waits until they answer, however long that takes. info returns at once.
Ask only what you can't find out yourself, and put related questions in one card. Send `info` rarely, only for what the person must know now.

The person is juggling many tasks and has lost the thread. In plain words, say what the work is for (the outcome, not the file), what just happened, and what you need. For a decision, give the options and what each one means. Pane already shows which Pane and agent sent it.

With no open call the reply reaches your tab as a `reply:` line, recorded the same way; `correction:` lines fix how it was taken. --took returns {took, id, next?}. Only the reply's reader may run took and update: the asker, the orchestrator that relayed it, or Autopilot. Anyone else gets ERR_NOTIFY_NOT_READER.
A result of {waiting: true, id} means the question is still on screen and your client would otherwise time out: call `notify` with resume: <id> right away to keep waiting. After 15 minutes on this loop Pane gives up and returns unavailable.
A result of {unavailable, next} means nobody can answer through Pane right now (Pane is not running, Notify is off, or the wait ended): ask in the terminal instead. It is a result, not an error.
Inside a Pane terminal the question names its Pane and panel (PANE_SESSION_ID and PANE_PANEL_ID); elsewhere it names the working directory.
An older Pane ignores links and shows the card without them.
With relays the call waits on the worker's card as on any notify, and the answer also goes straight to the worker's tab as `answer: Q-n → <answer> (by you)`. tools.name: todos_snooze
tools.title: runpane todos snooze
tools.description:
Snooze a to-do until a time: its agents stop after their current step, and Pane wakes them then with your note.
Use it to check something later (after a deploy, or for a reply) instead of waiting in a turn. At the time Pane sets the to-do back to In progress, restarts its orchestrator in the same conversation if it is down, and types the note. With --remind-me, or when the to-do has no Session, Pane raises a reminder card for the person instead. Snoozing a snoozed to-do changes its time and note. A time without an offset is read in this machine's zone; `snooze.until` is ISO 8601 with its offset in `snooze.zone`.
Snooze only a top-level to-do that is To do, In progress or Stopped. A sub-to-do, or one In review, Accepted, Done or Dropped, is refused with `todo_snooze_state`; a past time with `todo_snooze_past`; text runpane can't read, or a time more than a year out, with `todo_snooze_time`.
Comments on a snoozed to-do are held and go with the wake-up message. Writing to it (comment, attach, check) doesn't wake it; `todos_wake` does.
Returns the JSON of `todos_snooze`.

tools.name: profiles_launch
tools.title: runpane profiles launch
tools.description:
Launch a profile: Pane runs its workflow step by step, the first step in a new Pane of a Session.
Starts a run of the profile: Pane makes (or joins) a Session, opens the first step as a tab in a new Pane of the repo, and follows the workflow from there. Each agent step ends when its agent runs `report` with outcome: "<outcome>" (in the "agents" toolset) with one of the step's declared outcomes, a command step when its tab exits, and an ask when the person answers its card. Returns the run: id, sessionId, paneId, state, step and wait.
A launch without --prompt fails with ERR_PROFILES_PROMPT_REQUIRED and starts nothing.
Pane refuses a profile it cannot launch: PROFILE_NOT_FOUND (no such profile), PROFILES_OFF (Profiles is off in Settings › Advanced), PROFILE_TEAM_ONLY (no flow) or PROFILE_NOT_LAUNCHABLE (invalid, or off); the error's next says what to do.
A --harness or --agent-harness CLI that Pane doesn't know needs --command <cli>=<command that starts it>; without one the launch fails with PROFILE_CLI_UNKNOWN and starts nothing.
Follow the run with `profiles_runs`; its steps are tabs in the run's Pane (`agents_status` with pane: <paneId>).
Returns the JSON of `profiles_launch`.
